items.item_text: High school diploma or equivalent experience.
One (1) year of acute care hospital or post-acute care experience.
Knowledge and experience with community resources.

The Placement Coordinator serves as a key member of the Clinical Case Management team and is responsible for facilitating timely and appropriate post-acute care transitions through comprehensive referral management, placement coordination, authorization support, and transportation arrangements. Working collaboratively with Clinical Case Managers, physicians, nursing, post-acute providers, and community partners, the Placement Coordinator manages post-acute referrals, ensuring patients are transitioned to the appropriate level of care while minimizing discharge delays and supporting optimal patient outcomes.

The Placement Coordinator functions as a liaison between UCDH, post-acute providers, placement agencies, payers, and interdisciplinary teams to ensure efficient communication, coordination, and follow-through of post-discharge services. This role is responsible for managing referral workflows through a referral management system, obtaining post-acute authorizations, coordinating patient transportation through a system integrated in the electronic medical record, supporting difficult-to-place patients, and identifying resources that facilitate safe and timely discharges. The Placement Coordinator contributes to departmental initiatives focused on patient throughput, length-of-stay reduction, and care transitions.
5% - Education, Professional Development and Interpersonal Skills
Knowledge of all payer systems, procedures, and regulations including Medicare, Medi-Cal, Managed Care, and Third Party.

Knowledge of post-acute placement settings, including SNF, ARU/IRF, LTACH, Subacute, and CHLF facilities, with an understanding of admission criteria, payer requirements, placement barriers, and coordination of patient transitions to appropriate levels of care.
Knowledge and skills to obtain authorizations for post-acute care.
Ability to multi-task, set priorities, organize and work independently.
Ability to recognize and maintain confidentiality of patient information and comply with all HIPAA laws.
Ability to read, write, speak and understand English language and be able to utilize Medical Interpretation Services.
Ability to be prompt and meet deadlines for timely hospital discharges.
Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with widely diverse groups, including individuals at all levels both within and outside the organization and gain their cooperation.
Knowledge of Microsoft Teams, Outlook, EMR/Epic and CarePort or similar systems.
